subject: SIG: encryption controls — KMS/HSM process snapshot request

Subject: SIG: encryption controls — KMS/HSM process snapshot request

Hi Camila,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG review for the upcoming Q4 audit we need a concise "process snapshot" describing Redwood's encryption controls specifically for: in-transit encryption, at-rest encryption, KMS/HSM usage, and key rotation. We don't need your full SIG pack yet — just the following artifacts to move forward with our security team: 

- A short playbook or diagram that shows how keys are generated, stored, and rotated (granularity: CMKs, DEKs, KEKs).
- A sample rotation log (recent 6 months) showing timestamped rotations and who/what initiated them.
- A clear statement on whether Redwood's managed KMS uses HSM-backed modules and the FIPS level of those modules.
- Any BYOK options and the onboarding checklist for customer-managed HSMs.

Target turnaround: Oct 5 (auditor requested). If you can provide a minimal bundle (PDF + CSV sample + architecture diagram) that should be sufficient for the first pass. If there are any restrictions on sharing logs, please flag them up front.

Regards,
Sara Bennett
Security Program Manager
Acme Financial

Attachments: none (requesting artifacts)
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-28T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: encryption controls — KMS/HSM process snapshot request

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha (Security) and Aditya (Crypto Ops) to help assemble the artifacts. High-level notes below and we'll attach a short playbook and sample CSV in the follow-up message.

Quick answers up front: 
- In transit: All customer traffic to Redwood endpoints is TLS 1.2+ with enforced strong ciphers, mTLS available for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- At rest: Model and customer data at rest are encrypted using envelope encryption (per-customer data keys encrypted by CMKs in our KMS).
- KMS/HSM: Our managed KMS leverages HSM-backed key wrapping provided by our cloud KMS partners; we can provide HSM attestation details.
- Rotation cadence: Operational CMKs (root-of-trust) rotate on a 12-24 month cadence, DEKs rekeyed per retention policy or on deploy; customer-facing rotation options (BYOK) are available on request.

We will attach:
- redwood-kms-playbook-v1.pdf (process diagram + roles)
- kek-rotation-sample-202609.csv (redacted timestamps & identifiers)
- redwood-encryption-architecture-diagram.png

If anything needs to be redacted for privacy/contract reasons let us know and we'll provide an alternate sample. Delivering full SIG pack will follow after this snapshot.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-kms-playbook-v1.pdf (application/pdf), redwood-encryption-architecture-diagram.png (image/png)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-29T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: encryption controls — KMS/HSM process snapshot request

Hi Sara — adding a few operational specifics that the auditors typically ask for: 

- Key hierarchy: We use a three-tier model (KMS CMKs -> KEKs for service-layer wrapping -> DEKs per-customer or per-tenant). KEKs are rotated programmatically; DEKs are re-encrypted when KEKs change.
- Rotation triggers: scheduled cadence + manual triggers for suspected compromise + policy-driven rotation on tenant offboarding.
- Access controls: KMS admin actions require MFA + RBAC. Key rotation APIs are gated behind a key-ops role; rotation operations are auditable with immutable logs.
- HSM details: For the managed deployment we rely on cloud KMS HSM modules (provider-managed). For BYOK customers who provide their own appliances, we accept modules validated to at least FIPS 140-2 Level 2 and recommend Level 3 for hardware custody scenarios.

I'll attach the short playbook Camila mentioned and a redacted rotation CSV. The CSV includes rotation timestamps, rotation_type (scheduled/manual), initiator (system/user-role), and key_id (redacted).

Neha Kapoor
Director, Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kek-rotation-sample-202609.csv (text/csv)

Hi Sara / Procurement — responses below and attached items.

1) FIPS attestation: Our managed KMS providers publish module validation statements. For the managed offering we use HSM modules with FIPS 140-2 validation (provider-level documentation attached as vendor-attestation.pdf). Where customers use BYOK with their own hardware, we accept modules validated at FIPS 140-2 Level 2+; for scenarios requiring hardware custody we recommend Level 3 and can include that guidance in onboarding.

2) Signed cover letter: yes — attaching a one-page cover letter on Redwood Inference letterhead stating that the rotation CSV is a redacted sample exported from our immutable audit store and has not been modified.

3) PII in CSV: confirmed redacted. The rotation CSV includes pseudonymous key IDs and no customer-identifying PII. If your auditors need a notarized package or an in-person review, we can coordinate via your audit request form.

Attachments included in this email (stubs):
- redwood-kms-playbook-v1.pdf (process playbook; contains roles, flow diagrams, and rotation procedures)
- kek-rotation-sample-202609.csv (redacted sample; rotation_type, timestamp, initiator, key_hash)
- redwood-encryption-architecture-diagram.png (architecture diagram)
- vendor-attestation.pdf (public vendor HSM validation statements)
- redwood-rotation-coverletter-20261002.pdf (signed cover letter)

If that bundle looks good I can escalate to Legal for any additional attestation language your auditors require. Let us know by EOD Oct 5 and we will proceed.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference, Inc.
